title: Inventory and Radiators
premise: Ulyana Quintana, once a piano prodigy who vanished from the conservatory at nineteen, returns fifteen years later as a janitor, hiding in plain sight among the radiators and practice rooms where their career ended. At the funeral of Marta Quintana—the woman who raised them—a stranger named Elias Voss claims kinship through a family name no one has spoken aloud: the Voss line, which means Ulyana's inheritance, and the truth of what happened the night they stopped playing, belongs to a history Marta spent her life burying. As Ulyana cleans the halls they once conquered, they must decide whether loyalty to the dead woman's silence is worth more than the truth that could restore their music and claim the estate. The novel ends with Ulyana performing Marta's unfinished composition at the conservatory's centennial concert—naming the Voss name publicly, losing the inheritance to Elias, but reclaiming the family that actually chose them.
about_author: Ines Sterling is the pen name of a former conservatory custodian turned writer whose essays on labor and art have appeared in small literary journals. They live above a closed piano shop and write in the mornings before the building wakes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Keys
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Fifteen years after walking out mid-recital, Ulyana mops the conservatory's corridors at dawn, memorizing which practice rooms hold talent and which hold grief. When news arrives that Marta Quintana has died, Ulyana finishes the shift before allowing themselves to cry. Emotional beat: the cost of chosen invisibility.

chapters.title: A Stranger Wears the Name
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the funeral, a composed stranger introduces himself as Elias Voss, cousin by blood, and uses a surname Ulyana has never heard Marta speak. The mourners' confusion mirrors Ulyana's own dawning vertigo. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under a carefully built life.

chapters.title: What the Will Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Reading Marta's will, Ulyana finds the house left to them but a sealed envelope left 'to whoever can prove the Voss line.' Elias produces documents; Ulyana produces only silence. Emotional beat: inheritance as a test Ulyana never studied for.

chapters.title: Radiators and Repertoire
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Back at work, Ulyana bleeds air from a radiator in Studio C—the room where everything ended—and catches themselves playing phantom scales on its pipes. A young student, Noor, hears and asks for lessons. Emotional beat: the body remembers what the mind refuses.

chapters.title: Elias at the Door
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias visits the house, courteous and surgical, cataloguing Marta's belongings and probing Ulyana about 'the incident.' He offers partnership: share the truth, split the estate. Ulyana declines without explaining why. Emotional beat: charm as a weapon, and the first real threat.

chapters.title: Marta's Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Searching for tax papers, Ulyana finds a locked drawer containing an unfinished manuscript titled 'Voss Variations' and a newspaper clipping from fifteen years ago with a paragraph cut out. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion—what was Marta hiding?

chapters.title: Noor
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Sixteen, ferocious, and broke, Noor bribes Ulyana with coffee for unofficial lessons after hours. She doesn't recognize Ulyana's name, which is exactly why Ulyana says yes. Emotional beat: found family beginning, disguised as a transaction.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Using janitorial access, Ulyana pulls fifteen-year-old recital programs and discovers their final performance was replaced in the records by another student's name—edited by someone with authority. Emotional beat: the past was not just painful; it was doctored.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Itemized
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana confronts Marta's oldest friend, Ruth, who admits Marta erased the record to protect Ulyana—from what, she won't say. 'Some truths are gifts,' Ruth insists. 'Some are debts.' Emotional beat: loyalty reframed as something that can smother.

chapters.title: Elias Makes His Case
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias reveals he grew up on stories of the brilliant Voss child who disappeared, and that his own life collapsed in the shadow of that myth. He wants recognition more than money—or so he claims. Emotional beat: the antagonist becomes painfully legible.

chapters.title: The Cut Paragraph
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the library's microfilm, Ulyana reads the excised paragraph: a review naming Marta—not as mother, but as the teacher accused of driving the Voss prodigy to breakdown. Marta wasn't Ulyana's savior. She may have been the cause. Emotional beat: betrayal reordering fifteen years of gratitude.

chapters.title: Almost Saying It
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Drunk on cheap wine, Ulyana nearly tells Noor everything, then deflects into a story about a fictional pianist. Noor sees through it and says, 'You talk like someone rehearsing.' Emotional beat: the art of almost saying it, caught red-handed.

chapters.title: Break-In
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana returns home to find the drawer forced open and the Voss Variations gone. Only Elias knew it existed. Emotional beat: violation, and the realization that silence protected no one but the thief.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Cornered, Ruth confesses: Marta was Ulyana's aunt, not mother; the Voss parents died in a fire Marta believed she caused through negligence; she took the child and scrubbed the name to outrun guilt. Emotional beat: the whole architecture of Ulyana's life revealed as an apology.

chapters.title: The Centennial Committee
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The conservatory plans a centennial concert honoring its 'lost genius,' anonymously. The director asks Ulyana, as staff, to help curate archival material—including the restored record of the vanished student. Emotional beat: the institution itself begins undoing Marta's erasure.

chapters.title: Elias's Recital
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias performs the stolen Voss Variations at a private salon, claiming them as family heritage, and invites the conservatory director. Ulyana attends incognito and hears Marta's unfinished phrases completed badly—but recognizably. Emotional beat: watching your inheritance performed by a stranger's hands.

chapters.title: Confrontation in Studio C
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana corners Elias in Studio C and plays the variations correctly from memory, proving lineage more surely than any document. Elias, shaken, admits he stole the manuscript out of desperation—he's bankrupt, and the name was all he had. Emotional beat: rivalry collapsing into shared orphanhood.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Owes the Dead
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana visits Marta's grave intending rage and instead reads the headstone inscription Marta chose: 'She kept the fire.' Ulyana understands at last—Marta's silence was both crime and penance—and decides the truth deserves daylight anyway. Emotional beat: forgiveness without absolution.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The director offers Ulyana the centennial slot to perform the completed Voss Variations under their own name, restoring the record. Accepting means public exposure, professional risk, and betraying Marta's lifelong wish. Ulyana says yes. Emotional beat: choosing truth over the safety of invisibility.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor turns pages as Ulyana rehearses, witnessing their teacher transform from janitor back into musician—hands shaking, then steady. Noor demands the truth and finally receives it, all of it. Emotional beat: found family sealed by honesty rather than secrecy.

chapters.title: Centennial
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Before a full hall, Ulyana performs the Voss Variations and speaks the name aloud—claiming Marta's guilt, love, and gift in one breath. Elias watches from the last row; the estate goes to him uncontested. Emotional beat: climax—truth offered freely costs less than truth hoarded.

chapters.title: Inventory
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Weeks later, Ulyana still cleans the conservatory—by choice now, teaching Noor in the evenings—and takes inventory of what remains: a radiator that sings when played, a drawer left unlocked, a name used without flinching. Emotional beat: resolution—invisibility traded for belonging, on Ulyana's own terms.
